jobs.title: Senior Director AI and Transformation
jobs.description:
A career as a Senior Manager Artificial
Intelligence (AI) and Technology in the Capital Markets and Treasury risk
Management team at National Bank means playing a key role in transforming risk
management through AI. You leverage your leadership, technological expertise
and ability to build high-performing teams to have a concrete impact on the
organisation.
Your job

Define and implement the strategy and operational model for the AI
Talent Hub, including priorities related to talent, mandates, technology
and knowledge sharing.

Recruit, develop and engage AI specialists in automation, data,
product management and engineering, while maintaining a solid talent pool.

Deploy specialists or multidisciplinary teams with experts in
order to target opportunities with high added value, develop prototypes
and determine solutions to industrialise, transfer, rethink or abandon.

Guide the development and adoption of platforms, components, agent
models, methods and reusable development environments, in collaboration
with technology teams.

Support risk management leaders in developing their processes,
roles, skills, team structures and workforce needs.

Design and test governance approaches adapted to AI-assisted work,
in collaboration with the Technology, Cybersecurity, Data, Privacy, legal
Affairs, Compliance, Model risk and Architecture teams.  

Your team

Within the Capital Markets and Treasury risk
Management sector, you will lead a new multi-disciplinary team and report to
the Senior Vice-President. The Hub supports the various sectors and risk
management specialists. This team stands out for its technical excellence,
curiosity, mobility and close collaboration with various experts. The Hub helps
attract and circulate talent, accelerate promising initiatives, develop
reusable capabilities and transfer solutions to the teams best positioned to
develop them.
The Bank values continuous development and
internal mobility. Our personalised training programs, based on on on-the-job
learning, help you master your profession and develop new fields of expertise.
Tools such as the Data Academy, language training, the Harvard Learning Centre
and coaching and mentoring support are available to you at any time.
Prerequisites

University degree in computer science, engineering, data science,
a quantitative discipline or a related field, and significant relevant
experience.

Significant experience in creating and developing
multidisciplinary teams and leading large-scale organisational
transformations.

Solid applied knowledge of AI, agentic systems, automation, modern
software development, data and technology platforms.

Mobilising small teams to resolve complex and ambiguous business
problems.

Experience in financial services, risk management or a regulated
environment, an asset.

Languages: French, English
Reason to require this language: you will need to work closely with our colleagues outside Quebec.
Required skills: Business Alignment, Critical Thinking, Data-Driven Decision-Making, Decision Making, Diversity & Inclusion, Emotional Intelligence, Innovation Management, Learning Agility, Mobilization, Partner Development, Resiliency, Risk Management, Strategic Vision, Strategy Execution, Stress Management

Your benefits

In addition to competitive compensation, upon hiring you’ll be eligible for a wide range of flexible benefits to help promote your wellbeing and that of your family such as:

* Health and wellness program, including many options
* Flexible group insurance
* Generous pension plan
* Employee Share Ownership Plan
* Employee and family assistance program
* Preferential banking services
* Involvement in community initiatives
* Telemedicine service
* Virtual sleep clinic

We have an offer that keeps up with trends as well as your needs and those of your family.

Our dynamic work environments and cutting-edge collaboration tools foster a positive employee experience. We value employees’ ideas. Whether through our surveys or programs, regular feedback and ongoing communication are encouraged.

Making a bold move in a people-first environment

We’re a bank on a human scale that stands out for its courage, entrepreneurial culture, and passion for people. Our mission is to have a positive impact on people’s lives. Our core values of partnership, agility, and empowerment inspire us, and inclusion is central to our commitments. We aim, wherever possible, to provide a barrier-free and accessible environment to all employees.

We strive to provide accessibility measures throughout the recruitment process within the limits of our available resources. If you require accommodations, feel free to let us know during our initial conversations. We welcome all candidates! What can you bring to our team?

Join us!

jobs.title: AVP, Corporate Strategy & Enablement
jobs.description:
You are as unique as your background, experience and point of view. Here, you’ll be encouraged, empowered and challenged to be your best self. You'll work with dynamic colleagues - experts in their fields - who are eager to share their knowledge with you. Your leaders will inspire and help you reach your potential and soar to new heights. Every day, you'll have new and exciting opportunities to make life brighter for our Clients - who are at the heart of everything we do.

At Sun Life, we're driven by our Purpose: helping our Clients achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives. Our values shape how we work: caring, authentic, bold, inspiring, and impactful.

When you join Sun Life, you'll work with passionate colleagues and empowering leaders who support your growth and celebrate your contributions, so you can make a meaningful difference in our Clients' lives.

Discover how you can make a difference in the lives of individuals, families and communities around the world.

Job Description:

The Corporate Strategy & Enablement Team’s focus is to support Sun Life in achieving and maintaining a position of sustainable strategic advantage and growth in the long term. It has a broad focus on enterprise topics that span all Business Groups and geographic markets where Sun Life operates.

The AVP, Corporate Strategy & Enablement will report to the VP, Corporate Strategy & Enablement. The AVP will be responsible for ongoing delivery of internal strategy design and execution, and the annual strategic planning cycle, working effectively with teams across Sun Life to deliver strategy projects and proactively monitor and analyze trends. The successful candidate will work in a fast-paced, team-first environment with a focus on driving strategy and enablement project delivery, engaging senior leaders across Sun Life to solve key strategic questions/issues and structuring quantitative and qualitative analysis to solve critical strategic questions. The AVP will manage a small high performing team, acting as a coach and mentor through project work and team development opportunities.

What will you do:

Strategy development and planning:

Translate ambiguous issues into clear problem statements and hypotheses
Conduct quantitative (e.g., financial modeling, market sizing) and qualitative (e.g., benchmarking, expert synthesis) analysis
Develop and execute analysis plans using internal and external data sources

Strategy and enablement project delivery:

Define scope, design approach, and lead execution of strategy projects
Manage all project workstreams and coordinate across team members to ensure timely delivery
Present findings and facilitate discussions with senior management, including implementation planning

Trends and competitive intelligence:

Monitor industry trends, competitor actions, and market developments
Curate insights and identify implications for Sun Life’s strategy
Proactively share relevant patterns and themes with internal stakeholders

Communication and stakeholder engagement:

Effectively communicate insights, ideas, and strategies clearly & concisely to an executive level audience
Develop and maintain cross-functional relationships across the organization to identify emerging needs and opportunities
Facilitate working sessions with senior executives, including Sun Life’s Executive Team

People leadership and team development:

Manage a team of high-performing Directors & Senior Consultants
Mentor team members through apprenticeship and coaching
Foster a collaborative and learning-oriented team culture
Contribute to the development and success of the team and our practices

What do you need to succeed:

10+ years of relevant business experience, ideally within insurance or financial services
Strong understanding of at least one Sun Life business area (e.g. asset management, insurance, wealth management) and geographic markets (Canada, US, Asia)
Excellent communication, analytical and problem-solving skills
Strong interpersonal skills; able to effectively collaborate with multiple stakeholders across multiple teams
Able to work independently on assignments with appropriate judgment
Ability to coach team members on projects, providing guidance on analysis and deliverables
Proven ability to lead and develop a small team of high-performing professionals, including guiding project execution, driving accountability, and conducting performance and career development conversations

The Base Pay range is for the primary location for which the job is posted. It may vary depending on the work location of the successful candidate or other factors. In addition to Base Pay, eligible Sun Life employees participate in various incentive plans, payment under which is discretionary and subject to individual and company performance. Certain sales focused roles have sales incentive plans based on individual or group sales results.

Diversity and inclusion have always been at the core of our values at Sun Life. A diverse workforce with wide perspectives and creative ideas benefits our Clients, the communities where we operate and all of us as colleagues. We welcome applications from qualified individuals from all backgrounds.

Persons with disabilities who need accommodation in the application process, or those needing job postings in an alternative format, may e-mail a request to thebrightside@sunlife.com.

We are proud to be a hybrid organization that offers our employees the choice and flexibility to work from both the office and virtually based on the needs of the business, our Clients and you.

We may use artificial intelligence to support candidate sourcing, screening, interview scheduling.

We thank all applicants for showing an interest in this position. Only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

jobs.title: Director, Business Services and Corporate Governance
jobs.description:
The Director, Business Services and Corporate Governance provides leadership and oversight for centralized business services and corporate governance functions that enable organizational effectiveness, consistency and accountability across ASEBP. Working closely with the Chief Strategy and Governance Officer, the Director translates strategic direction into operational initiatives, ensures effective coordination across portfolios, and drives continuous improvement initiatives that strengthen organizational performance and governance.

This role provides operational leadership for four departments, including Trustee Governance, Communications and Marketing Services, Risk Services, and Business Delivery Services. The role involves working collaboratively with leaders across ASEBP to establish organizational standards, support strategic execution and strengthen corporate governance practices.

Your Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership for Business Support and Governance
Provide operational leadership for ASEBP's business support functions, including Governance, Communications and Marketing, Risk, and Business Delivery Services.
Establish standards, processes, templates and governance practices that support consistency across the organization.
Coordinate priorities, resources and work plans across portfolio functions to support effective service delivery and organizational outcomes.
Monitor service delivery, performance measures and operational outcomes, and identify opportunities to improve effectiveness and consistency.

Governance Planning and Support
Lead the development, implementation and maintenance of governance frameworks, policies and supporting processes.
Support organizational compliance with governance requirements, corporate policies and applicable standards.
Oversee governance reporting, tracking and documentation practices.
Coordinate support for executive, committee and trustee governance activities, as assigned.
Identify governance risks and recommend practical mitigation strategies.

Strategy and Operational Planning
Translate strategic direction from the Chief Strategy and Governance Officer into operational plans and priorities.
Coordinate portfolio initiatives, projects and organizational improvement efforts.
Monitor progress toward strategic objectives and provide reporting to senior leadership.
Facilitate business planning, resource planning and performance measurement activities.
Provide analysis and recommendations regarding organizational priorities, resource allocation and strategic execution.

People Leadership
Lead managers and professional staff within the portfolio.
Establish clear expectations, accountability measures and development plans.
Foster collaboration, inclusion, employee engagement and continuous learning.
Support succession planning and talent development within the portfolio.
Manage performance, workforce planning and organizational change initiatives.

Partnerships and Collaboration
Build strong partnerships with leaders across ASEBP.
Facilitate cross-functional problem solving and decision-making.
Provide strategic advice and recommendations to senior leaders.
Represent the portfolio on corporate initiatives and working groups.
Support organizational change management and communication activities.

Your Education and Experience

Completion of a university degree in business, public administration, governance or a related field. Completion of a Master's degree would be an asset.
A minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible leadership experience in governance, organizational effectiveness, business operations, corporate services, strategy execution or a related area.
A governance, project management, risk management, change management or leadership-related designation is considered an asset.
Experience supporting or working with a Board of Directors, Board of Trustees, executive committees, or similar governing bodies is considered an asset.

A combination of education and experience may be considered.

Your Abilities

Provide strategic and operational leadership in a complex and evolving environment.
Develop and implement governance frameworks, policies, standards and business processes that support organizational objectives.
Analyze complex organizational issues, assess risks, evaluate alternatives and develop practical solutions and recommendations.
Lead organizational change initiatives and build alignment across diverse stakeholder groups.
Establish priorities, allocate resources and manage multiple competing initiatives while balancing short- and long-term organizational needs.
Build collaborative relationships and influence decision-making across all levels of the organization.
Communicate, facilitate, negotiate and resolve issues effectively with internal and external stakeholders.
Interpret and apply legislation, governance requirements, policies and organizational objectives to support sound decision-making.
Lead, coach and develop leaders and professional staff while fostering a culture of accountability, inclusion and continuous improvement.
Leverage data, performance measures and business insights to evaluate outcomes and support strategic and operational decisions.

Unique Working Conditions

This position is eligible to participate in ASEBP’s hybrid workforce program.
Some travel within Alberta may be required.

If you have the required qualifications and would like to become a member of our team, please submit your application by November 9, 2026
.

No phone calls please. We thank all interested individuals, but only those candidates being considered for an interview will be contacted. ASEBP is an equal opportunity employer.

All offers of employment for this position are conditional upon satisfactory background and reference checks, which may include a criminal record check, and/or education and employment verification.

jobs.title: Director, Finance
jobs.location: St John’s, Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada
jobs.description:
Director, Finance, Provident10

St. John’s, NL

Are you a strategic, forward thinking finance leader ready to drive financial excellence, strengthen organizational performance, and make a lasting impact on the retirement security of thousands of Newfoundlanders and Labradorians?

The Company

Some would say we’re in the pension business. We like to say we’re in the people business. One that focuses on creating an inclusive and diverse culture for everyone who comes through our doors. One that puts our 68,000 members at the heart of everything we do because they deserve nothing less than a secure, stable future to build upon. One that can include YOU.

Provident10 is the largest pension plan in Newfoundland and Labrador and one of the largest pension plans in Atlantic Canada - representing 1 in 8 Newfoundlanders and Labradorians. Our team proudly oversees the pension administration and investment management of the over $13 billion Public Service Pension Plan Fund. Future Focused. People Centric. The foundation for our vision. For us that means creating a
seamless experience for members and a positive culture for our employees; ensuring the organization remains efficient and agile, as we continue to make smart investments for growth – all while embracing technology and ensuring a consistent experience for our members.

The Role

The Director, Finance is accountable for the leadership, management, and integrity of the corporate and investment fund finance function, including financial reporting, planning, controls, investment accounting, and transaction processing. The role ensures the delivery of accurate and timely financial information, robust internal controls, and compliance with applicable standards and regulatory requirements., The Director, Finance supports organizational decision-making through financial analysis and planning and provides operational leadership across all finance activities. The role serves as the primary internal authority on financial management and stewardship, while contributing to enterprise planning and supporting Board and committee reporting.

Key Responsibilities:

Financial Management & Reporting:
Oversees corporate and fund financial reporting, including fund accounting requirements and related financial statement preparation. Leads the preparation of quarterly, and annual financial statements and reports. Ensures accuracy, completeness, and timeliness of all financial reporting in accordance with applicable accounting standards. Oversees the financial close process, including general ledger integrity and reconciliations. Provides financial analysis and insights to support organizational performance and decision-making.

Investment Fund Accounting & Oversight:
Leads the organization’s investment accounting and financial reporting activities for the pension fund. Oversees portfolio reconciliation, investment valuation, performance reporting controls, and the integrity of investment-related financial information. Maintains oversight of investment accounting systems, private market reporting, management and performance fee monitoring, and foreign tax recovery activities. Ensures investment accounting processes are completed accurately, timely, and in compliance with applicable accounting standards, regulatory requirements, and internal policies. Supports Board and committee reporting by providing analysis and insights on investment-related financial matters.

Planning, Budgeting & Forecasting:
Leads the annual budgeting process, including the development, consolidation, and monitoring of both corporate and investment fund budgets. Works collaboratively with department leaders. Oversees ongoing forecasting activities, monitors financial performance through variance analysis and provides recommendations to support long-term financial planning and sustainability analysis.

Controls, Compliance & Risk Management:
Establishes and maintains a strong internal control framework. Ensures compliance with legislative, regulatory, and accounting requirements. Maintains oversight of applicable tax compliance, reporting, and related advisory requirements. Leads external audit processes and coordinates responses to audit findings. Develops and maintains financial policies, procedures, and governance frameworks.

Operational Finance Leadership:
Provides day-to-day leadership and oversight of the finance function. Ensures efficient and effective financial processes and identifies opportunities for improvement and automation. Maintains oversight of cash management, financial transactions, and organizational financial resources. Ensures appropriate segregation of duties and transactional controls across all finance activities.

Stakeholder Support & Advisory:
Supports in the development of Board and committee materials, including Audit & Finance Committee reporting. Provides financial guidance and decision support to leaders across the organization. Acts as a key liaison with external auditors and other financial stakeholders.

People Leadership:
Leads, develops, and mentors the finance team. Establishes clear performance expectations and supports professional development. Ensures appropriate resourcing and capability to meet current and future organizational needs.

The Ideal Candidate

You are a collaborative, member-focused leader who excels at breaking down silos and building high-performing cross-functional partnerships. You bring a track record of engaging diverse stakeholders, aligning priorities, and making thoughtful decisions that support the broader goals of Provident10. As a trusted advisor, you develop innovative, practical solutions to complex challenges while maintaining an unwavering commitment to service excellence and member needs.

You bring a strong foundation in financial reporting, governance, and stewardship, complemented by experience leading complex finance functions and supporting sound organizational decision making. Ideally, you have exposure to pension plans, institutional investment operations, fund accounting, or other complex investment environments. You understand the importance of robust financial controls, accurate investment reporting, effective oversight of external service providers, and the financial stewardship required to support a large long-term investment fund.

You foster a culture of continuous improvement by encouraging new ideas, sharing leading practices, and empowering others to think differently. Highly accountable and results-driven, you set clear goals, adapt resources and priorities effectively, and persist through obstacles to achieve outcomes. You communicate progress transparently, remove barriers to success, and inspire teams to deliver sustainable results that create value for members, customers, stakeholders, and the organization.

Qualifications and Experience

While the Search Committee recognizes that no one candidate is likely to meet all qualifications in equal measure, those listed below are desirable and will be used to compare candidates.

Undergraduate degree in Business, Finance, or a related discipline.
CPA designation.
8–12 years of progressive experience in finance, accounting, or related roles.
Demonstrated experience in financial reporting, budgeting, compliance and controls, and audit management.
Experience with pension plans, institutional investment management, investment fund accounting and reporting, investment operations, custodial arrangements, private-market investments, or other large and complex investment portfolios is considered a strong asset.
Proven leadership experience managing teams and finance operations

Skills and Attributes

Strong analytical and financial modelling capabilities.
Ability to translate financial information into actionable insights.
Strong communication skills with experience supporting senior leadership and governance bodies.
Knowledge / Strong knowledge of accounting standards and financial reporting requirements.
Expertise in internal controls, audit processes, and financial governance.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Data & Analytics
jobs.description:
Our Company Background & Culture

UPP is the first pension plan of its kind in Ontario’s university sector, proudly serving over 46,000 members across six universities and nineteen sector organizations. Our purpose is to bring greater retirement peace of mind to the university sector by investing with integrity and serving members with care. As a sector-wide plan designed for growth, our doors are open to all Ontario universities.
UPP is recognized as one of Greater Toronto’s Top Employers for 2026. Together, we’re a team of progressive thinkers and agile doers operating within a fast-paced culture of collaboration and respect. We believe in bringing smart and capable people together to create, solve, and grow with a clear shared vision and values of integrity, inclusivity, ingenuity, and impact.
Our culture is intentionally welcoming and purposefully rooted in equity, diversity, inclusion, and reconciliation (EDI&R). We believe diverse teams, perspectives, and lived experiences contribute to better decisions and a better workplace.
As a pension plan, UPP approaches investing through a long-term lens to generate and safeguard value. Our commitment to investing responsibly accounts for material risks that impact our investment portfolio to generate sufficient risk-adjusted returns to meet the pension needs of our members.
Join us in building a bright future for our members, our organization, and each other.
THE ROLE

We are seeking a forward-looking Senior Director, Data & Analytics to lead and evolve UPP’s enterprise data capabilities. Reporting to the Managing Director, Data and Technology, this role will work with business and technology leaders to improve how data is governed, integrated, managed and used across UPP. Its scope includes data in UPP’s enterprise data hub and across the broader cloud solutions ecosystem, including Google Cloud Platform (GCP). The Senior Director will help ensure data is trusted, accessible and fit for business reporting, analytics, automation and emerging AI workloads.
This is an opportunity for an experienced data leader to shape an important enterprise capability and help UPP make better use of its data as the organization grows.
This role is based in downtown Toronto under a hybrid work policy, allowing employees the flexibility to work remotely and in-office (two days per week in-office).
This posting is for an existing vacancy.
Specific Accountabilities

The Senior Director, Data & Analytics will lead and evolve UPP’s data capabilities, including the following:
Develop and evolve UPP’s enterprise data strategy and practices so data is well governed, reliable, discoverable and useful across the organization.
Lead and develop a high-performing team responsible for data quality, data engineering, data integration, data operations and analytics enablement.
Establish data standards and practices in partnership with business data owners, Architecture, Cybersecurity and other technology teams.
Guide the use of cloud-based data capabilities, including GCP, to support reliable data integration, reporting and analytics. Improve data quality, access, lineage and governance so data is ready for responsible automation and AI workloads, in partnership with the teams accountable for AI platforms, architecture, privacy and cybersecurity.
Partner with business and technology leaders to prioritize data needs and enable trusted, data-informed decisions. Establish the access patterns, tools, standards, training and controls that allow business users, including citizen data users, to work with data safely and at scale.
Improve the reliability, quality, reuse and maintainability of data integration and transformation flows that support key processes, including pension data conversion, regular employer reporting, and Finance reporting and analysis.
Leverage leading frameworks (such as DCAM) to continually mature and evolve the data strategy and frequently self-asses the capabilities for progress
Define and communicate data priorities, target capabilities and roadmaps, aligning plans with enterprise needs and available capacity.
Research and establish peer connections to understand industry trends and their applicability to support data plans and strategies for the enterprise
Explain the value of trusted data and sound data management practices to technical and non-technical audiences.
Oversee UPP’s data catalog and related metadata practices, working with Architecture and data owners to improve data discoverability and stewardship.
Contribute to UPP’s reputation as a respectful employer, partner, and participant in the financial sector

Qualifications & Experience

10+ years of demonstrated experience developing and leading enterprise data capabilities, including data governance, data engineering, integration, data operations and analytics.
CDMP (Certified Data Management Professional) or an equivalent qualification is an asset.
Significant progressive experience in data management, including data governance, architecture, integration, data quality, metadata and analytics.
Experience leading data teams or capabilities in a cloud-based environment, with sufficient technical understanding of data platforms, databases, integration and transformation tools, analytics and visualization to set direction and make informed decisions. Experience with GCP or comparable cloud data platforms is an asset.
Understanding of relational and non-relational data and the considerations involved in integrating and governing different data types.
Experience working across complex business domains; experience in pensions, investments or financial services is an asset.
Experience designing and evolving cloud-based data capabilities in partnership with internal teams and external service providers.
Working knowledge of analytics methods and the interpretation of quantitative information.

ATTRIBUTES

Excellent written and verbal communications
Ability to design and improve repeatable data practices
Ability to drive outcomes through collaboration across teams and contributors
Ability to engage and align business users, data owners and technology partners.
Ability to effectively identify emerging technologies, trends, standards, and products that have a strong potential to better enable UPP business units
Ability to enable consistent, governed data use at scale.

LIFE AT UPP

Do work that matters.
We are duty-bound to serve our members’ interests, and it’s a responsibility we don’t take lightly. That’s why we’ve ingrained sustainability in our work from day one—to ensure our members have a resilient future to retire into, both today and for generations to come.
Stronger together.
Collaboration is how UPP was born, and it’s how we work with each other and our partners day in, day out. No one at UPP is just a number (even if they are excellent at math) and every win is a shared win.
Grow every day.
You’ll have the opportunity to work on unique, once-in-a-career projects that maximize your skill set and probably teach you some new ones—at any stage in your career.
Prioritize wellness.
At UPP, wellness takes many forms. Ultimately, it’s about ensuring our people are cared for in the ways that matter to them. Check out some highlights of our inclusive employee-focused benefits program including:
Defined benefit pension plan
Flexible hybrid work model
Paid time off – vacations, personal days and wellness days
Work remotely up to eight weeks/year
Comprehensive group benefits including medical, dental, vision, etc.
Extended paramedical and mental health service coverage
Health care and lifestyle spending accounts
Fertility treatments, paid parental leave, and gender affirmation coverage
Education Assistance program

jobs.title: Senior Director, Financial Reporting
jobs.description:
Most financial reporting functions are measured by whether deadlines are met. That’s important, but this role gets to decide what excellence looks like while meeting deadlines.

With accountability for external reporting and technical accounting, the Senior Director, Financial Reporting will play a defining role in advancing the reporting function of a Canadian-headquartered public manufacturing company. Reporting to the VP, Finance, this leader will oversee the full reporting cycle and strengthen the processes, controls, technical expertise and team required to support its continued evolution.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who can deliver against current reporting requirements while strengthening the function for the future. The successful candidate will bring experience from a rigorous public company reporting environment and the judgment to apply that experience within a Finance organization that continues to evolve.

The Mandate

The Senior Director will have end-to-end responsibility for quarterly and annual public company reporting under IFRS, ensuring financial statements, disclosures and supporting documentation meet the standards required of a public company.

The role will also serve as a key technical accounting resource across Finance, providing guidance on complex and non-routine matters and ensuring accounting positions are well considered, documented and communicated.

Key responsibilities include:
Lead quarterly and annual public company reporting, including the preparation and review of external financial statements and disclosures under IFRS.
Own the reporting process from planning through review and completion, with clear accountability for quality, accuracy and timelines.
Provide technical accounting leadership across Finance, interpreting and applying IFRS to complex and judgmental matters.
Prepare and review technical accounting memos covering areas such as goodwill, impairment and significant accounting estimates.
Support potential US GAAP considerations and the requirements associated with a potential conversion.
Provide accounting support for M&A transactions, integrations and divestitures as they arise.
Lead reporting and technical accounting discussions with external auditors, ensuring issues are properly analyzed, documented and resolved.
Strengthen reporting processes, controls, documentation and review standards.
Identify opportunities to create greater consistency, efficiency and discipline across the reporting function.
Lead, coach and develop the team, including a planned Senior Manager, Technical Accounting hire.
Partner closely with Finance and Tax on accounting and reporting matters.
Build effective relationships with senior leaders and C-suite stakeholders, communicating complex issues clearly and credibly.

What You Bring

You are a CPA/CA with progressive public company financial reporting experience and strong technical accounting capability. You understand the discipline required in a public company environment and have experience taking ownership of a reporting process from beginning to end.

Your background includes:
CPA/CA designation, ideally with a foundation in public accounting.
Progressive public company financial reporting experience with direct ownership of quarterly and annual reporting.
Strong IFRS technical accounting expertise and experience applying guidance to complex accounting matters.
Experience preparing and reviewing technical accounting memos on significant, judgmental and non-routine issues.
The technical depth and judgment required to support potential US GAAP conversion requirements.
Experience working directly with external auditors and supporting accounting positions through clear analysis and documentation.
M&A-related accounting experience, including exposure to integrations and divestitures, considered a strong asset.
A track record of improving reporting processes, controls and standards.
Proven people leadership experience, including coaching, development and performance management.
Comfort working in a fast-paced environment where processes and capabilities continue to be refined.

How You Lead

You bring the technical credibility to navigate complex accounting matters and the business judgment to understand their broader implications. You are comfortable operating in the detail, but you know when to step back, engage others and move an issue toward resolution.

Your leadership is reflected in how you:
Establish and maintain a high standard for reporting quality.
Apply sound judgment when accounting guidance requires thoughtful interpretation.
Communicate complex matters clearly to audiences with varying levels of technical knowledge.
Build trusted relationships across the reporting team, Finance, Tax, external auditors and the C-suite.
Create accountability through clear expectations, ongoing feedback and meaningful coaching.
Develop people while addressing performance concerns directly and fairly.

The Opportunity

For someone who has developed their experience in a strong public company reporting environment, this role provides the opportunity to take on a broader leadership mandate within a manufacturing business headquartered in Canada.

The Senior Director will have the scope to improve how the reporting function operates, strengthen its technical accounting capability, develop the team and introduce the structure needed to support the organization as it evolves.

It is a role for a financial reporting leader who enjoys the rigor of public company reporting but also wants the opportunity to build, improve and leave the function stronger.

Apply in confidence.

jobs.title: Director, Strategic Finance - Remote in Canada
jobs.description:
DIRECTOR, STRATEGIC FINANCE

Who is a Director, Strategic Finance?

The Director, Strategic Finance is a high-impact leader within the Office of the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) who brings an investment-oriented perspective to GoodLife Group’s most consequential strategic, financial and enterprise-value decisions. This role personally leads complex analysis and selected cross-functional workstreams under the delegated authority of the CFO.

Reporting directly to the Chief Financial Officer, the role expands the capacity and analytical depth of the Office of the CFO across executive decision support, capital allocation, enterprise performance, Value Creation Plan validation, Apollo and Board engagement, financing and merger and acquisition (M&A) execution.

Working with leadership from across Financial Planning & Analysis, Accounting, Data & Analytics and Operations departments, the role influences through expertise, credibility and delegated CFO authority, while functional leaders retain ownership of their teams, source information and recurring processes.

What will you be doing?

Enterprise strategic finance, corporate modelling and capital allocation

jobs.description:
THE OPPORTUNITY

We have an exciting opportunity for a Director of Finance / Controller to join LITCO LSO, a growing organization with multiple entities. Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer and partnering closely with the Fractional Chief Financial Officer, this role provides leadership to the Finance and Accounting team while overseeing accounting operations, financial reporting, budgeting, audit coordination and finance activities across multiple entities.

This role is responsible for strengthening the accounting function, improving financial reporting, and establishing consistent finance processes. The position also supports acquisition integration and the ongoing development of financial controls, reporting standards and accounting practices across the organization.

THE IDEAL CANDIDATE

The ideal candidate is an experienced finance leader with a strong technical accounting foundation and demonstrated success leading accounting and finance functions within complex, multi entity organizations. This individual combines strong financial management, budgeting, audit oversight, and financial reporting expertise with the ability to establish structure, improve processes, and strengthen financial controls.

Comfortable working with senior leaders and strong personalities, this individual provides objective advice, constructive challenge, and practical solutions. Success in the role requires confidence, resilience, sound judgment, executive presence, and the professional maturity to communicate candidly, uphold strong financial practices, and navigate complex situations with credibility.

THE ORGANIZATION

Litco LSO is North America’s leading Legal Support Organization, partnering with high-performing law firms that share our commitment to excellence, innovation, and client-first service. Backed by institutional investors and built on a foundation of operational rigor, we provide the resources, infrastructure, and strategic guidance firms need to scale—without sacrificing their values or autonomy. Our platform includes shared services in finance, HR, IT, marketing, and compliance, freeing our partner firms to focus on what they do best: serving clients.

We’re redefining what it means to run a modern law firm. Whether through M&A integration, advanced technology, or culture-driven leadership, Litco helps legal teams move beyond outdated business models and toward a sustainable, future-ready approach. Our growing network spans multiple jurisdictions across Canada and the U.S., uniting like-minded firms under a shared mission: to build the most respected and forward-thinking legal organization on the continent.

For more information, please visit their website: www.litcolso.com

RESPONSIBILITIES

Financial Reporting & Accounting

Lead the organization’s accounting and financial reporting functions across multiple entities.
Oversee the preparation of consolidated financial statements and ensure consistent accounting practices.
Ensure the timely and accurate preparation of monthly, quarterly and annual financial statements.
Maintain effective accounting policies, controls and reporting standards.
Provide financial analysis and recommendations that support business performance and operational decision making.

Budgeting & Financial Planning

Lead the annual budgeting process and ongoing forecasting activities.
Monitor financial performance, analyze variances, and identify emerging risks and opportunities.
Lead monthly operating reviews with each business unit, partnering with executive leaders to review financial performance, budget variances, forecasts, and operational results in support of effective decision making.
Develop financial models and analysis to support planning, resource allocation, and organizational objectives.

Audit & Financial Oversight

Oversee the annual external audit process and act as the primary liaison with external auditors.
Coordinate audit planning, documentation, and the resolution of audit related matters.
Ensure financial policies, procedures, and controls are maintained and consistently applied.
Ensure compliance with applicable financial reporting, regulatory, and internal control requirements.

Mergers, Acquisitions & Integration

Support finance related activities associated with acquisitions and integrations.
Support finance due diligence and post acquisition integration activities, as required.
Assist in evaluating and integrating financial processes across acquired entities.
Promote consistency in financial reporting, controls, and accounting practices across multiple entities.

Systems & Process Improvement

Lead or support the implementation, optimization, and enhancement of financial systems and reporting tools.
Identify and implement opportunities to improve efficiency, accuracy, and effectiveness within the finance function.
Support technology and process improvement initiatives that strengthen financial management and operational effectiveness.

Leadership & Stakeholder Collaboration

Provide leadership, direction, and mentorship to the Finance and Accounting team.
Build and strengthen the team through coaching, mentoring, and succession planning.
Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
Build effective working relationships with senior leaders and key stakeholders.
Communicate financial information clearly, confidently and effectively to a variety of audiences.

QUALIFICATIONS

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce, Business Administration, or a related discipline.
CPA designation required.
Strong technical accounting foundation with experience preparing consolidated financial statements.
Minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in finance and accounting, including experience leading finance and accounting functions within a complex organization.
Demonstrated experience overseeing budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, and year end audit activities.
Experience working within organizations that operate across multiple entities, business units, or corporate structures.
Demonstrated experience supporting mergers, acquisitions, and integration activities.
Experience leading and developing finance and accounting teams.
Experience supporting financial systems implementations, technology-enabled process improvements, or organizational transformation initiatives is considered an asset.
Strong understanding of accounting principles, financial reporting, financial controls, and financial management practices.

KEY COMPETENCIES

Demonstrates strong financial and business acumen, using analysis and sound judgment to support effective organizational decision making.
Communicates with confidence, credibility, and executive presence, effectively presenting financial information, recommendations and business insights to senior leaders and C-suite executives.
Builds trusted relationships and provides objective advice and constructive challenge, demonstrating the confidence and professional maturity to work effectively with senior leaders, strong personalities, and diverse stakeholder groups.
Exercises professionalism, discretion, and sound judgment when managing sensitive issues and competing priorities.
Leads teams through accountability, mentorship, and clear expectations, fostering a culture of engagement and performance.
Identifies opportunities to improve processes, strengthen controls, and enhance operational effectiveness.
Comfortable establishing structure and adapting to changing priorities in a growing organization.
Adapts effectively to changing priorities and organizational needs while maintaining a practical, solutions focused approach.
Demonstrates integrity, accountability, and professionalism in all aspects of leadership and financial stewardship.
